mintAuthorityControl.question: Does the shipped two-sided delta actually reject the four failure shapes?
mintAuthorityControl.v3GrantNeverLanded: REJECTED — positive assertion on the runtime address in BOTH _phase7_phlimboV3Assertions (:2397-2402) and the verifier (:266-275), checked against the CURRENT mintVersion so an inert grant is caught
mintAuthorityControl.v2RevokeNeverLanded: REJECTED — but NOT by the mask. With baseline bit 19 clear (verified live), `baseline & ~v2Bit == baseline`, so the delta degenerates to the old invariance check and cannot distinguish a landed revoke from an absent one. It is caught unconditionally by the separate absolute assertion at :2421-2426. The control is sound; the delta is simply not the thing that catches this case today, and the verifier logs an explicit NOTE (:259-263) rather than implying otherwise.
mintAuthorityControl.verdict: The control is INTACT and honestly documented. The lens-1 hypothesis that the delta assertion dies quietly over a no-op revoke is NOT borne out — no finding filed on it.
mintAuthorityControl.residualScope: The mask only sees 20 compile-time addresses plus the 15 swept runtime deployments; a grant to anything else is invisible. Pre-existing from story 075, unchanged here — parked as MR-24-02.

guardTestSuite.result: 9 passed / 0 failed (run by me: `forge test --match-path test/PhusdMinterDeltaGuards.t.sol`)
guardTestSuite.doesItTestWhatItClaims: Substantially yes, with a disclosed limitation. Six tests exercise a LOCAL RE-MODEL of the mask assertion (`_assertExpectedDelta`), not the shipped verifier — the file's own header says so explicitly and gives the reason (instantiating the script would need live mainnet at every inherited constant). Three source-level tests pin the shipped code against drift: the `PHUSD_MINTER_BIT_PHLIMBO_V2 = 19` constant and `require(i == 20,`; the presence of the positive V3 assertion together with the ABSENCE of `_requireNotPhusdMinter(newPhlimboV3` and the PRESENCE of `_requireNotPhusdMinter(migratorV2V3`; and the literal `phusdMinterMaskAtPhase0 & ~v2Bit` plus `phusdMintVersionAtPhase0`. Those string pins are what stop the model and the shipped assertion drifting apart, and they are well chosen. The honest caveat: a semantically equivalent rewrite of the shipped expression would break the pins (noisy but safe), while a change that keeps the literal substring and alters surrounding logic would not be caught.
guardTestSuite.notable: test_oneSidedCheckWouldBeVacuous_twoSidedIsNot demonstrates the downgrade it exists to prevent, which is the right way to write this test.

localPassOrdering.property: ForgeLocalPassPrecedesBroadcast (established run-23; documented for this suite in the :verify npm doc key and in VerifyPromotionReady's header)
